title: Lute project declaration document (state/defs/enums/entities)
description: STRUCTURE-only schema for a Lute project declaration doc (dsl §9.2/§9.3, data-catalog foundation A3/B4): the `.yaml` form (B4) of what is today a kind-less `.lute` frontmatter block imported via `uses:`/`extends:`. Mirrors `crates/lute-check/src/meta.rs::{UNIVERSAL_KEYS,parse_meta_kind}` (top-level keys, `state:`), `crates/lute-manifest/src/entities.rs` (`enums:`/`entities:`), and `crates/lute-manifest/src/types.rs::TypeDef` (the `type:` tagged forms). Does NOT validate CEL body validity, state-path resolution, or domain membership — those stay in the Lute checker (B3).

plugins.description: Plugin id -> option overrides (untyped at this layer; option shapes are plugin-declared).

state.description: dsl §9.3: dotted state path -> declaration. Path tier/segment validity is semantic (checker), not shape.

defs.description: dsl §8.1 / 0.21.0 §7b defs: name -> declaration, either the shorthand CEL string or the long-form mapping (def_decl.rs::lift_def; anything else is E-DEF-DECL).

entities.description: 0.3.0 draft §3.1: entity kind -> closed member list or engine-open marker.

cast.description: dsl 0.23.0 §7, 0.24.0 §4: speaker id -> `{ name?, present?, emotions?, assume? }`. Once any cast is declared (here or by a plugin's `cast` export), a content line whose speaker is outside it is `E-CAST-UNKNOWN`.

present.description: dsl 0.24.0 §4: the CEL condition under which this speaker is present (`holds(inParty(isolde))`). A line by the speaker whose enclosing guards do not imply it is `W-CAST-ABSENT`.

emotions.description: dsl 0.24.0 §4: the `emotion=` values this speaker takes; any other is `E-BAD-ENUM`.

assume.description: dsl 0.24.0 §4: `true` — presence reads every negated `holds` of an engine-`reserved` relation in `present` (directly or through a rule: `inParty(P) :- …, not fell(P)`) as holding, i.e. assumes the engine has not written it. Lines after the engine event then need their own guard.

clock.description: dsl 0.24.0 §1 (lute-manifest clock.rs::ClockDecl): the project's one clock, over existing engine-owned state paths. `lute play` `advance:` moves it; content reads the reserved `clock.index` / `clock.weekday` / `clock.weekdayLabel`; scene beats take `once: day|slot`, entries `once="day"|"slot"`. Path ownership, slot/enum agreement and week consistency are semantic (`E-CLOCK-DECL`), not shape.

day.description: the day path — a `number` state path declared `owner: engine`.

slot.description: the slot path — an enum state path declared `owner: engine`. Omit it (and `slots`) for a clock that counts whole days.

slots.description: the slot order within a day; exactly the slot enum's members, each once.

raise.description: one occasion raised after every advance, where the clock stops — or a map of moments: `slot` (the same), `dayEnd` (at every midnight an advance crosses, before it), `dayStart` (after it).

first.description: the 0-based weekday index of day 1 (default 0; below `length`).

labels.description: one display label per weekday (exactly `length`); read as `clock.weekdayLabel`.

refList.description: `uses:`/`extends:`/`components:` accept a single ref or a list (meta.rs::get_ref_list).

enumsMap.description: entities.rs::parse_enums — vocabulary slot name -> members, each becoming a closed ordered Domain. dsl 0.9.0 D-F moved content-vocabulary MEMBERS out of the compiler (`lute.core/enums.yaml` is `enums: {}`), so this block is where a project declares its own; using a slot nobody declared is `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN`.

enumDecl.description: schema.rs::EnumDecl (untagged: `Members(Vec<String>)` | `Long { members, default, exits }`) and the equivalent hand-rolled shapes in entities.rs::parse_enums. A bare sequence is shorthand for `{ members: [...] }` (dsl 0.9.0 D-D), so every pre-0.9.0 declaration keeps validating. `members` is REQUIRED in the long form — it carries no `#[serde(default)]`, and parse_enums SKIPS an entry whose `members:` is missing rather than declaring an empty closed domain. `default:`/`exits:` are optional HERE by design: dsl 0.9.0 requires `exits:` on the `action` slot and `default:` on `anchor`, but that rule is keyed to the slot NAME and to which slots a project declares, which no positional JSON Schema can express — `lute check` owns it and reports it. Unknown keys are closed even though serde IGNORES them: a typo'd `exit:` would silently drop the stage-exit semantics with no diagnostic from any layer, which is exactly what an editor schema is for.

labels.description: dsl 0.24.0 §1: member -> display text a `{{…}}` interpolation of a value of this enum renders. Every key must be a member (`E-ENUM-LABEL-NOT-MEMBER`); a member without a label renders its id.

entityDecl.description: relations.rs::parse_entity_kinds — `{ members: [...] }` (closed, optionally `subsetOf: <kind>`), `{ open: <any> }` (engine-populated; the VALUE is never inspected, only key presence), or dsl 0.26.0 §2.3 `{ add: [...] }` alone (members added to the kind one other schema import declares). Neither key present silently produces no domain in Rust — flagged here as a real shape mistake.

inlineDefDecl.description: dsl 0.21.0 §7b (def_decl.rs::lift_def): the shorthand `name: "<CEL>"`, or the long form `{ type?, params?, cel }`. `cel` is required; an absent `type` is inferred from the body; `params` requires `type`. Any other key is E-DEF-DECL.

params.description: dsl §8.1 `params:` (schema.rs::de_params) — a MAPPING `{ p: <Type> }` (source-order preserved) OR a SEQUENCE of `{ name, type }` entries (the plugin defs.yaml list spelling).

shape.description: A record field MAY reference a named shape instead of an inline `type:`.

literal.description: types.rs::Literal — untagged: bool | number | string | list | map (string keys).

type.description: types.rs::TypeDef — the plugin §7 Type wire form. Bare unit tags (`bool`/`number`/`string`) or a SINGLE-key tagged map (`serde_yaml::with::singleton_map_recursive` requires EXACTLY one key to resolve the variant, hence `additionalProperties: false` + `required` per branch below).

oneOf.description: dsl 0.26.0 §2.5: a member of a project entity kind (`entities:`); attribute types.
